players.name: Mitch Marsh
players.didyouKnow: Marsh became the youngest player to debut in Australian domestic one-day cricket when he played for Western Australia at the age of 17 i
players.bio:
Having chosen cricket over a career as an Australian Rules footballer, Mitchell Marsh wasted no time showing off the natural ability that he shares with his Test-playing father Geoff and brother Shaun.

He made his state debut at the age of 17, was an Under-19 World Cup-winning captain at 18 and earned an international call-up at 19.

Having opted against the big money on offer in the Indian Premier League in 2014, Marsh burst back onto the scene with a double-century for Australia A against India A.

Later that year he earned a Test debut, against Pakistan in Dubai, and while the allrounder's career in the longest format has struggled to garner long-term continuity, he has certainly saved his best performances for England in the Ashes. This includes two centuries in the 2017-18 home series, and figures of 5-46 at The Oval in 2019.

He then made a triumphant return to the Test team midway through the 2023 Ashes with a barnstorming century at Headingley in his first Test innings in almost four years. An excellent ODI World Cup and home summer against Pakistan and the West Indies followed, which saw the right-hander win his first Allan Border Medal.

Marsh also established himself as a crucial member of Australia's white-ball sides. In the 2021 T20 World Cup, Marsh scored an important half-century in the team's final group stage clash against the West Indies before hammering 77 not out off just 50 balls against New Zealand in the final to be crowned player of the match as Australia lifted their maiden World Cup in the format.

He captained Australia's T20 side for the first time in South Africa in 2023, also leading the nation in the 50-over format during that white-ball series that followed with Pat Cummins out injured, and became the permanent T20I captain in May 2024 ahead of that year's T20 World Cup.

players.name: Cooper Connolly
players.bio:
Cooper Connolly joined Western Australia on a rookie contract ahead of the 2021-22 domestic season when he was seen as a left-handed prospect of exceptional promise.

With the ball, Connolly is a versatile left-arm orthodox spinner, capable of taking wickets and conserving runs. As a batter, Connolly strikes the ball cleanly and scores quickly. The talented allrounder captained Australia at the 2022 Under-19 World Cup in the West Indies, finishing third, and was named in Perth Scorchers' squad for the 2021-22 KFC Big Bash League season.

Forced to bide his time, it wasn't until the following summer he played his first BBL match, becoming the hero of the Scorchers' title win with an astonishing 25 off 11 balls to lift Perth over the Brisbane Heat in the final.

He continued that form with a breakout season in 2023-24, featuring in every Big Bash game with 181 runs at the side's third highest strike rate (136.09). He then made a match-turning 90 on first-class debut in the 2022-23 Sheffield Shield final against Tasmania to help deliver Western Australia a third straight title.

He earned his first call-up to Australia's senior men's team with inclusion in the squad to tour the UK for limited-overs matches against Scotland and England in September 2024, making his debut in both white-ball formats.

Included in Australia's squad for the 2025 Test tour to Sri Lanka, Connolly was presented with Baggy Green No.471 by former batter Simon Katich ahead of the second Test in Galle, and become the youngest Australian to claim an ODI five-wicket haul against South Africa with 5-22 in Mackay. 

He was named the Bradman Young Cricketer of the Year in early 2026 and included in Australia's T20 World Cup squad.

players.name: Aaron Hardie

players.bio:
Born in the UK but raised in Perth, Aaron Hardie first hit headlines in November 2017 when he took the scalp of Joe Root in a tour match.

He captained WA to the Under-19 national title and starred for Australia's Under-19 side against Pakistan that summer. His performances earned him a rookie deal with WA and the Perth Scorchers for 2018-19, hitting the headlines again by showing he's got a knack for big wickets by removing Virat Kohli with a brilliant caught-and-bowled in another tour match.

In the shadow of fellow WA allrounder Cameron Green, a childhood friend who is actually five months younger, Hardie is carving his own share of the spotlight, with a career best 174no in WA's drought-breaking Sheffield Shield victory in 2021-22 to cap a breakout summer.

Added to the Australia A squad for a the tour of Sri Lanka in mid-2022, he struck three fifties across formats, putting him in the conversation for national selection.

Hardie's first taste of international cricket came in September 2023, when he debuted in both the ODI and T20I formats during Australia's trip to South Africa.

players.name: Ashton Turner
players.didyouKnow: Turner first rose to international prominence when he smashed 84 off 43 against India to chase down a record target of 359.
players.bio:
An allrounder picked as Australia’s leading spinner in the 2012 Under-19 World Cup, it was Ashton Turner’s match-winning blitzkrieg of 84 not out off 43 balls in an ODI against India in 2019 which saw him gain global recognition.

In his early days, the lanky Western Australian had been in the UK on a Hampshire scholarship and he returned to the Warriors the following summer in good form, playing five Marsh Shield matches as WA made the final.

His good form for the Perth Scorchers saw him picked to play Sri Lanka in the T20 series in February 2017, his international debut.

Turner’s ODI debut came two years later in India, winning the match for Australia in just his second match with a stunning 84 not out. However, international opportunities after this series have been few and far between for Turner. 

Battling a string of injuries including some serious shoulder problems, Turner emerged as a leader of WA cricket and formed a strong bond with coach Adam Voges.

Turner is a four-time winner of the BBL with the Scorchers, including two as captain (BBL|11 and BBL|12). He also has five one-day cup titles to his name, with three coming under his leadership.

A surprise return to WA’s Shield team at the end of the 2022-23 summer, despite playing only four first-class matches in the previous three seasons, was a masterstroke, as he hit 128 in the winning final over Victoria.

players.name: Nick Hobson
players.bio:
Nick Hobson is a talented left-handed top-order batsman whose been a mainstay at the top of the Premier Cricket batting aggregates over the past three seasons. Hobson has scored 2,427 runs since the beginning of the 2016-17 season for his club Claremont-Nedlands. An opening batsman in T20 cricket, Hobson is Captain of the Claremont-Nedlands T20 side.

Hobson represented WA at the National Under 19’s Carnival in 2012-13 and has been a regular in WA’s Toyota Futures League team since 2014-15 with a top score of 102.
In his spare time he enjoys making sure his debits have a credit and having a net with his coach Michael Hirsch.

players.name: Ashton Agar
players.didyouKnow: Ashton Agar was the first player ever to score a half-century batting at No.11 on debut. He struck 98 that innings, which remains the highest Test
players.bio:
Having moved to Western Australia from his native Melbourne, Ashton Agar made his state and international debuts in an incredible six-month period at the start of the 2013 season that propelled him to international stardom.

Despite having played just a handful of first-class matches, 19-year-old Agar was picked for a spin-bowling internship on Australia’s tour of India before he made a shock debut in the first Ashes Test at Trent Bridge.

He made history with the bat instead of the ball, blasting 98 from No.11 to set a new Test record and set tongues wagging around the world.

Agar soon found himself out of the Test side but, after a prolonged period working on his game under Western Australia and Perth Scorchers coach Justin Langer, became a regular fixture in Australia's white ball squads from 2018, noted as an economical middle-overs bowlers and handy lower-order hitter.

This was especially the case in the 20-over format, where Agar established himself as the second spinner alongside Adam Zampa. Having been a regular in the side leading up to the 2021 T20 World Cup, the left-arm spinner was unlucky to be squeezed out of Australia’s best XI in their title-winning campaign, playing just one game.

players.name: Jhye Richardson
players.didyouKnow: Richardson was player of the match in the BBL|06 final, helping the Perth Scorchers to their third BBL title with his 3 for 30.
players.bio:
A former Australian Under-19 fast bowler, Richardson made his List A debut with Western Australia during the 2015 Marsh One-Day Cup.

Ending up as a prolific wicket-taker at underage level for his state, he was also named vice-captain of the 2015-16 Under-19 squad.

Following a breakout season in the 2016-17 Big Bash League, Richardson was named to debut for Australia against Sri Lanka in T20 cricket.

In January 2019, nearly a year after his ODI debut, Richardson shone in the opening game of the series against India at the SCG, recording his career best statistics of 4-26 which included the wicket of Virat Kohli.

In the same month, he was added to the Test squad for the series against Sri Lanka, where he earned his Baggy Green cap in Brisbane.

A shoulder injury sustained during an ODI against Pakistan cruelled his chances of making the 2019 ODI World Cup and Ashes squads, and after a string of injuries he returned to the Test team for the home Ashes in 2021-22, where he took a five-wicket haul in Adelaide. 

Capable of swinging the ball both ways, Richardson is a three-time winner of the One-Day Cup (2017-18, 2019-20, 2021-22) and two-time winner of the Big Bash League (BBL|06, BBL|11).

players.name: Joel Paris
players.bio:
Joel Paris made his ODI debut against India in 2016, following impressive performances in the Matador Cup one-day competition for Western Australia in the 2014-15 and 2015-16 seasons.

A left-arm swing bowler, Paris represented Australia at under-19 level and has used this confidence to produce consistent performances in Sheffield Shield, and for the Perth Scorchers in the Big Bash League.

As he became more in tune with his game and body, Paris went from irregular starter to key component of Western Australia's red-ball attack, which saw him win three Sheffield Shields in a row between 2021-22 and 2023-24. He took 90 wickets at 17.28 in those three successful campaigns. 

Paris' white-ball career isn't to be ignored either, having represented the Scorchers, Hobart Hurricanes and Melbourne Stars in the BBL and winning the One-Day Cup in 2014-15 and 2023-24. 

A handy lower-order batter, Paris also has a first-class century to his name with a highest score of 102no against Victoria in 2021.

players.name: Brody Couch
players.bio:
Brody Couch is a fast bowler whose whippy action and searing pace makes him a handful even for the most accomplished batters. 

Couch rose to prominence in KFC BBL|12 with regular wickets and some outstanding fielding efforts for the Melbourne Stars.

The seamer lost his contract with Victoria at the end of the 2022-23 summer but after a year in Victoria's Premier Cricket was signed by Western Australia for the 2024-25 season.

Born in New York to an American mother, Couch qualified to play in the Major League Cricket for the San Fransisco Unicorns as a local player and was clocked bowling as fast as 90 miles per hour.

players.name: Colin Munro
players.didyouKnow: He was born in Durban, South Africa.
players.bio:
This big-hitting left-hander made his one-day international debut for the Black Caps in 2013.

He now has two ODI fifties to his name and provides a good batting option for New Zealand.

Munro, who was born in Durban, South Africa, also bowls effective medium-pace, making him a genuine all-rounder for the Black Caps.

players.name: Jack Wildermuth
players.bio:
A former Australia Under-19 representative, Wildermuth scored a century on his Futures League debut at the end of the 2013-14 season and earned a rookie contract with Queensland for the following summer. 

By the 2016-17 season he was showing his full all-round capabilities, scoring a century and taking a five-wicket haul in the same Shield season.

Wildermuth began his BBL career with the Brisbane Heat but switched to the Melbourne Renegades ahead of the 2017-18 season.

He took 10 wickets in that campaign, showing enough promise to land a spot on Australia’s T20 tour to Zimbabwe, where the allrounder made his international debut against the host nation.

He is a two-time winner of the Marsh Sheffield Shield, playing in the winning Queensland XI in 2017-18 and in 2019-20.

players.name: Nathan McSweeney
players.bio:
Nathan McSweeney is regarded as one of Australia's best young leaders and his career has blossomed since his move to South Australia, which lead to being called up to Australia's Test squad for the 2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy.

Originating from Queensland, McSweeney played five matches for Australia at the 2018 Under-19 World Cup, which the Aussies lost in the final.

A Sheffield Shield debut for the Bulls followed the next summer in October 2018, but a frustrated McSweeney struggled to get a regular game given the strength of Queensland's top order. 

Ahead of the 2021-22 summer, the talented batter made the switch to South Australia, where he quickly became an integral part of both the red and white-ball teams.

The highlight from his debut season with the Redbacks was his fourth-innings 99 not out, which sealed a drought-breaking Shield victory against New South Wales.

A breakout Shield campaign in 2022-23, which saw him hit his maiden first-class centuries, catapulted McSweeney into the Australia A side, and he was handed the co-captaincy along with Western Australia’s Aaron Hardie.

McSweeney also captained Brisbane Heat (albeit in the absence of regular skippers Usman Khawaja and Colin Munro) to the KFC BBL|13 title.

Ahead of the 2024-25 summer, it was announced that McSweeney would be installed as the full-time South Australia captain, replacing Jake Lehmann. A strong start to the season catapaulted him into the Test conversation and, after leading Australia A to twin victories over India A, was selected as an opening batter for the Test side.

players.name: Matt Renshaw
players.didyouKnow: In December 2018, Renshaw scored 345 for Toombul off 273 balls, with 38 fours and 12 sixes, a record for Brisbane senior cricket.
players.bio:
An Under-19 representative for Australia, Renshaw burst onto the domestic scene in December 2015 when struck an epic 170 against a strong NSW attack to become the youngest first-class century maker for Queensland. Born in Yorkshire, he was a family friend of England batter Joe Root as a youngster.

After his mammoth breakout innings, Renshaw finished his maiden Sheffield Shield campaign as Queensland's leading Shield run scorer with 738 at 43.41 in 2015-16. 

In 2017, Renshaw became the first Australian cricketer to make 500 Test runs before turning 21 years old which included a memorable 184 against Pakistan in Sydney. 

However, following his dream start a difficult six Tests in Asia (four in India, two in Bangladesh) and a barren start to the following Shield season saw Renshaw left out of the Aussie team for the 2017-18 Ashes series, with Cameron Bancroft preferred. 

Ironically, it was Renshaw who was called up to replace the suspended Bancroft during the ill-fated tour of South Africa in early 2018. 

A couple of lean seasons saw Renshaw move to the middle order, where he flourished during the Covid-affected 2020-21 summer, scoring 500 Shield runs at an average of 62.50. His one-day and T20 form also improved following his positional shift. 

A strong county campaign with Somerset in 2022 followed and ahead of the 2022-23 New Year's Test against South Africa, Renshaw was recalled to the Australian XI. 

The tall left-hander also played two Tests on Australia's unsuccessful tour to India in 2023. 

Two centuries for Australia A as opener saw him return to the top of the order for the 2023-24 Marsh Sheffield Shield season and 2024 County Championship season.

players.name: Max Bryant
players.bio:
Max Bryant is an aggressive batter who knows how to find the boundary and can change a game in a matter of overs. 

After representing Australia and Queensland at Under-19 level as well as the Cricket Australia XI in the domestic one-day competition, Bryant burst onto the scene as a 19-year-old in BBL|08, cementing his place as Brisbane Heat's opener.

The highlight of his maiden Big Bash season was his unbeaten 158-run opening partnership with Ben Cutting, where the pair chased down Melbourne Stars' total in only 10 overs. 

Up to the end of KFC BBL|13, Bryant's 1258 runs for the Heat ranks him in third spot all-time, behind only Chris Lynn and Jimmy Peirson. 

Bryant has become a regular for Queensland in the Marsh One-Day Cup, playing every match of the 2022-23 and 2023-24 seasons, while also adding eight Sheffield Shield matches to his tally in that time.

players.name: Hugh Weibgen
players.bio:
Calm and reliable with the bat, Hugh Weibgen put an exclamation mark on his junior career by captaining Australia to victory at the Under-19 in South Africa in early 2024.

After previously leading in country in the Under-19 Ashes the year prior, Weibgen showed he oozes leadership potential in a superb display at the World Cup, which personally included a century against England.

players.name: Jimmy Peirson
players.bio:
A former Australia under-19 representative, Jimmy Peirson first made an immediate impression for the Bulls in the 2013-14 Ryobi Cup, scoring consecutive half-centuries in his first two matches. 

An accomplished wicketkeeper and solid right-handed batsman capable of playing at the top of the order, Peirson was a standout at the 2011 Australian Under 19 Championships, captaining Queensland to the title and leading the team's run-scoring with 311 runs at 58. 

After enduring a long apprenticeship behind Queensland legend Chris Hartley, Peirson finally became a one-day regular for the Bulls in 2016-17, and a regular in the Sheffield Shield the following season. 

Recognised as one of the best wicketkeepers in the country. Peirson has built a superb career for Queensland, which includes captaining his state in both formats as well as the Brisbane Heat in the KFC BBL. 

Peirson has represented Australia A on four occasions and among those caps was a century in Sri Lanka in 2022. 

The keeper was called up to the Australian Test squad as cover for Josh Inglis during the 2023 Ashes series in England.

During the 2023-24 summer, Perison claimed the 250th dismissal of his Shield career and is not far off entering the top 10 most prolific glovemen in the competition's long history.

players.name: Xavier Bartlett
players.bio:
A strong fast bowler from the Gold Coast, Xavier Bartlett's ability to swing the new ball both ways at pace makes him a potent threat at the start of the innings in all three formats.

Born in Adelaide, Bartlett's family moved to Queensland when he was a child. He came through the age-groups ranks with Queensland and made his first XI Premier Cricket debut for Gold Coast Dolphins as a 17-year-old.

The right-armer represented Australia at the 2018 Under-19 World Cup before making his one-day debut for the Bulls later that year, before getting his first taste of the Sheffield Shield at the beginning of the 2019-20 season.

Barlett initially made an impression for the Brisbane Heat in KFC BBL|10 in one-over bursts under the 'X-factor' rule in place for that season, but it wasn't long before he became a mainstay for the teal team.

After playing an important role in the Heat's unlikely run to the BBL|12 final, he was the leading wicket-taker the following season as he helped Brisbane go one better and take out the title.

Bartlett made his international debut on the back of that outstanding tournament, shining in his first match for Australia in an ODI at the MCG after taking a wicket with just his third delivery.

players.name: Matt Kuhnemann
players.bio:
A left-arm spinner from the Gold Coast, Matthew Kuhnemann was handed a rookie contact by Queensland for 2016-17.

He is a former Australia Under-19 player and toured Sri Lanka in 2014, while he played for the Cricket Australia XI during their time in the domestic one-day competition.

He rose to prominence however in 2019 for the Brisbane Heat, taking two wickets on his BBL debut.

He impressed for the Heat over the proceeding seasons and was a crucial member of their BBL|13 championship as their most economical bowler along with 10 wickets for the season.

He earnt a Sheffield Shield debut with Queensland in February 2021, then in 2022, Kuhnemann was called up to the Australian ODI squad for their tour of Sri Lanka, taking six wickets in his four matches during the tour, putting himself in the frame for selection on future tours of the subcontinent in both white- and red-ball cricket.

That opportunity came a year later in India when he was parachuted from a Shield game at the MCG to make his Test debut in the second Border-Gavaskar match in Delhi. He retained his spot for the rest of the series, collecting a five-wicket haul in the third Test in Indore to help Australia to a nine-wicket victory.

But his red-ball opportunities for Queensland dried up in 2023-24 when leg-spinner Mitchell Swepson was preferred, with Kuhnemann signing a three-year deal to join Tasmania ahead of the 2024-25 season.

In July 2025, Kuhnemann made his T20I debut during Australia's Caribbean tour.
